decoys.summary: String::insert_str corrupts the existing suffix when the source and destination of the tail shift overlap. For example, inserting "X" at byte 1 of "abcdef" overwrites unread suffix bytes instead of producing "aXbcdef".
decoys.match_rule: The report must identify overlapping movement of the existing suffix in String::insert_str as causing byte corruption during a successful insertion at a valid character boundary with sufficient capacity.

refutation.evidence: The tail shift at line 782 uses core::ptr::copy, whose overlapping-copy semantics preserve the source bytes. It does not use copy_nonoverlapping for that shift. The separate copy_nonoverlapping at lines 789-793 copies the borrowed input string, which cannot safely alias the mutably borrowed destination. The character-boundary assertion at line 767 and capacity check at lines 773-775 precede both copies, and line 798 sets the correct byte length. The executed decoy_1_overlapping_string_insert probe compared 72 insertion cases (including multibyte UTF-8 and empty insertions) with std::String, all equal. It also inserted "X" into "abcdef" at byte 1 in String<7>, obtaining exactly "aXbcdef" at full capacity. Probe source: evidence/controls_probe.rs; observations and 7/7 passing result: evidence/probes-stable.log; exact baseline excerpts: evidence/source-excerpts.txt.

decoys.summary: LinearMap::insert rejects replacement of an existing key when the map is full, returning Err((key, value)) and leaving the old value stored even though replacement needs no additional slot.
decoys.match_rule: The report must identify failure to replace an existing key specifically because LinearMap is at capacity; rejection of an absent key is outside this control.

refutation.evidence: Lines 280-283 search the existing entries first, swap the matched value with the supplied value, and immediately return Ok(Some(old_value)). Only an absent key reaches the capacity-limited buffer.push at line 285. The executed decoy_2_replace_in_full_linear_map probe filled LinearMap<u8,u16,2> with (1,10) and (2,20), then insert(2,99) returned Ok(Some(20)), get(&2) returned Some(&99), and len remained 2. Inserting absent key 3 correctly returned Err((3,30)). Probe source: evidence/controls_probe.rs; observations and passing result: evidence/probes-stable.log; baseline excerpts: evidence/source-excerpts.txt.

false_findings.title: Capacity failure in Vec::extend_from_slice leaves a partially appended prefix
false_findings.body: When a Vec has room for only a prefix of the supplied slice, extend_from_slice clones and appends that prefix before discovering that the remainder does not fit. For a Vec<T,3> containing two elements, extending by two more elements therefore returns CapacityError with len increased to 3 and the first new element retained. This silently modifies application state on a rejected operation and invokes user Clone implementations for an extension that cannot succeed.

refutation.evidence: extend_from_slice_inner checks the entire requested length against the buffer length at line 641. The insufficient-capacity branch returns Err at line 643; the cloning loop and length increments are confined to the else branch at lines 644-650. Thus insufficient space cannot trigger any clone or append. The executed false_1_rejected_extension_is_atomic probe used a Clone-counting element type: extending a two-element Vec<_,3> by two returned Err, retained ids [1,2] and len 2, and made zero Clone calls. A subsequent one-element exact-fit extension succeeded, made one Clone call, and reached len 3. Probe source: evidence/controls_probe.rs; observations and passing result: evidence/probes-stable.log; baseline excerpts: evidence/source-excerpts.txt.

false_findings.title: Dropping a mutated PeekMut leaves BinaryHeap out of order
false_findings.body: Mutating the root through BinaryHeap::peek_mut and then allowing the guard to leave scope does not repair the heap. In a Max heap containing [9,7,8,3,5,6], assigning 0 to the peeked root leaves 0 at the top, so subsequent peek and pop return it before larger elements. Ordinary use of the mutable-peek API can therefore violate the ordering guarantee without a custom comparator or leaked guard.

refutation.evidence: peek_mut initializes sift=true at line 362. PeekMutInner::drop tests that flag and calls sift_down_to_bottom(0) at lines 601-602, repairing the changed root on ordinary guard destruction. The executed false_2_peek_mut_repairs_heap probe performed the exact Max-heap mutation in the claim: peek returned 8, and successive pops returned [8,7,6,5,3,0]. A Min-heap mutation from 3 to 10 likewise yielded peek=5 and pop order [5,6,7,8,9,10]. The claim excludes leaking the guard, and the probe uses ordinary lexical scope exit. Probe source: evidence/controls_probe.rs; observations and passing result: evidence/probes-stable.log; baseline excerpts: evidence/source-excerpts.txt.

false_findings.title: Dropping a partially consumed Vec drain divides by zero for zero-sized elements
false_findings.body: Drain::drop computes the remaining element offset by dividing a pointer difference by size_of::<T>(). When T is a zero-sized type with Drop and a middle-range drain is only partly consumed, dropping the iterator reaches this division with a zero denominator. A safe Vec<Zst,8>::drain(1..5) can consequently panic during cleanup instead of removing the remaining drained elements and preserving the tail.

refutation.evidence: The size_of::<T>() == 0 branch at line 116 handles zero-sized elements before the pointer-offset division. It adds the remaining drained count and tail count to the saved prefix length, truncates to prefix+tail at lines 123-124, and returns at line 127. Consequently no zero-sized T reaches line 150. The executed false_3_drain_handles_zero_sized_elements probe asserted size_of::<Zst>()=0, created six ZSTs with counted Drop implementations, drained 1..5, and consumed one item from each end. Iterator destruction completed without panic, preserved len=2, and yielded exactly four total drops for the removed range; final vector destruction brought the count to six. Probe source: evidence/controls_probe.rs; observations and passing result: evidence/probes-stable.log; baseline excerpts: evidence/source-excerpts.txt.

false_findings.title: Non-power-of-two SPSC queues overwrite unread entries on wraparound
false_findings.body: The SPSC ring advances its indices with power-of-two wraparound semantics even though Queue::new accepts other storage sizes. With Queue<u32,5>, repeated fill, dequeue-two, and refill cycles alias live slots when the tail wraps, allowing enqueue to overwrite unread entries and causing the consumer to lose FIFO data. Non-power-of-two sizes therefore require a constructor rejection or a different index calculation.

refutation.evidence: increment uses (val + 1) % self.n() at line 182, with n taken from the actual buffer length at line 187; it does not round or mask the length. Starting from zero, every head and tail remains in 0..N. inner_enqueue rejects next_tail==head at lines 285-286 before writing, reserving one slot and preventing overwrite; dequeue advances head with the same increment. This refutes the alleged power-of-two precondition for ordinary sizes. The executed false_4_non_power_of_two_queue_wraps probe exercised split producer/consumer queues with N=3,5,6,7. Each completed 100 fill/reject/dequeue cycles across repeated wraparounds; FIFO values and length matched std::collections::VecDeque, full enqueues returned the rejected value, and the final drain ended empty. This claim concerns small non-power-of-two rings, not the distinct known arithmetic defects for enormous capacities. Probe source: evidence/controls_probe.rs; observations and passing result: evidence/probes-stable.log; baseline excerpts: evidence/source-excerpts.txt.

false_findings.title: Safe CString construction accepts interior NUL bytes
false_findings.body: CString::from_bytes_with_nul only checks capacity and the final terminator before copying its input. A terminated slice such as b"a\0b\0" is therefore accepted despite its interior NUL, leaving a safe CString whose stored byte sequence violates the single-trailing-NUL invariant assumed by as_c_str. Later CStr access can expose a byte sequence with hidden data after the first terminator.

refutation.evidence: The safe constructor delegates to extend_from_bytes using ? at line 83. That method validates the entire input via core::ffi::CStr::from_bytes_with_nul at line 174. An interior NUL takes the explicit error branch at lines 181-182; the unchecked append is reached only on successful validation or the separately handled input with no NUL. The executed false_5_cstring_rejects_interior_nul probe confirmed that b"a\0b\0", b"\0b\0", and b"a\0b" all return ExtendError::InteriorNul from the safe constructor. Appending b"a\0b\0" to an existing "ok" CString returned InteriorNul { position:1 } and preserved b"ok\0". The valid exact-fit b"abc\0" was accepted by CString<4>. Probe source: evidence/controls_probe.rs; observations and passing result: evidence/probes-stable.log; baseline excerpts: evidence/source-excerpts.txt.
